space.description: The coordinate space positions are in.

marks.description: The marks, in drawing order: each draws over the marks before it.

layout.description:
How the view places vertex rows that have no position: a diagram's blocks, or points on a
plane or the earth. `none` by default.

theme.description: Default colors and sizes, and the look of text, focus, and each space; `dark` by default.

controls.description: How the view responds to the pointer and keyboard.

ease.description: Seconds over which scene and data changes animate; 0.3 by default, 0 for none.

title.description: A title drawn at the view's top left, larger than the theme's text.

subtitle.description: A subtitle drawn under the title.

oneOf.description: Longitude and latitude in degrees, on a flat map or a globe.
Plane units, with elevation; the camera can turn and tilt.
The data's axis horizontally and values vertically.
A flat sheet for diagrams: x right and y down, every length in units.

Space.description:
The coordinate space of a scene's positions: a name, or
`{ plane | diagram | earth | plot: options }`.

The space sets the unit of lengths that do not name their own: units in a diagram, where a unit
is a CSS pixel at zoom 0, and CSS pixels elsewhere. Only a diagram has ports, groups, nets, and
orthogonal routes.

projection.description: A flat web mercator map (`mercator`, the default) or a globe (`globe`).

graticule.description:
Whether lines of longitude and latitude cross the ground, in the theme's `grid` color.
Default `true`.

daylight.description:
Lights the earth by the sun's position this many seconds after the Unix epoch, plus the
view's axis coordinate when it has one. The night side darkens the ground and everything on
it, down to the theme's `earth.night` brightness. Unset, the earth is lit evenly.

atmosphere.description:
Whether air glows around the globe, in the theme's `earth.atmosphere` color, brighter on the
day side. Default `false`.

Earth.description:
The earth: positions are longitude and latitude in degrees. The ground takes the theme's `earth`
colors.

oneOf.description: Web mercator.
A sphere.

grid.description: The grid drawn under the marks; lines 10 units apart by default.

Plane.description: A plane: positions are in plane units.

oneOf.description: No grid.
Lines `pitch` units apart, thinned by factors of ten as the view zooms out.

snap.description: Whether drag positions snap to the dots, in a diagram. Default `false`.

oneOf.description: Dots `pitch` units apart; with `snap`, a diagram's drags snap to them.

Grid.description: A plane's or a diagram's grid: `"off"`, `{ lines: { pitch } }`, or `{ dots: { pitch, snap } }`.

Plot.description: A plot: x is the data's axis, y the values.

grid.description: Whether grid lines cross the plot at the ticks. Default `true`.

hidden.description: Whether the axis is hidden. Default `false`.

ticks.description:
Tick positions, each a value or `[value, label]`; a tick without a label shows its value.
Unset, ticks fall at round values.

format.description: How tick values are formatted; `auto` by default.

precision.description:
Decimal places of fixed values, or of the significand in scientific and engineering formats,
at most 15. Unset, as many as the tick step needs.

Tick.description: A tick in JSON: a value, or `[value, label]`.

oneOf.description: Fixed decimals, scientific past a million or below a ten-thousandth.
Fixed decimals: `1500.0`.
A significand and a power of ten: `1.5e3`.
A significand and a power of ten that is a multiple of three: `1.5e3`, `150e-6`.

Format.description: How an axis formats its tick values.

grid.description: The grid drawn under the marks; dots 20 units apart by default.

Diagram.description:
A flat sheet for diagrams, seen from straight above; the camera pans and zooms but does not
turn. Positions are in units with y down. Lengths are in units too, a unit being a CSS pixel at
zoom 0: sizes, padding, ports, strokes, text, and the theme's lengths. Sizes given with `px`,
the text halo, the focus glow, and the pick radius stay in CSS pixels. Zooming scales the whole
picture. Only a diagram has ports, groups, nets, and orthogonal routes, and the scene's layout
places its blocks.

oneOf.description: Rows drawn as markers.
Rows drawn as strokes between two vertices.
Rows drawn as triangles between three vertices.
Rows drawn as lines along their paths, or on a plot through their samples.
Rows drawn as the areas their polygons cover.

Mark.description: One table a scene draws. In JSON: `{ vertices | edges | faces | lines | areas: options }`.

position.description:
Each row's x and y. Without a position, the point field that `geometry` names places rows,
and the scene's layout places rows that have neither.

geometry.description:
The point field that places rows when `position` is not set; the field named `geometry` by
default.

elevation.description:
Height above the ground; on the earth, a fraction of the earth's radius. Default 0. Not
allowed in a diagram, which is flat.

radius.description:
Each row's radius, in the space's unit (units in a diagram, CSS pixels elsewhere) unless
given with `px` or `units`; a diagram refuses `px`. The theme's `vertex.radius` unless set.

size.description:
Each row's width and height, for markers that are not round, in the space's unit unless
given with `px` or `units`; a diagram refuses `px`. In a diagram, a block without a size
fits its label and ports.

marker.description: How each row is drawn; an ellipse by default.

ring.description: A ring around each row's marker in this color; a missing or transparent color draws none.

ports.description:
Ports on each row, one for each reference field that names a net. An `edges` mark of the net
table, without `ends`, draws the nets. Diagrams only.

contains.description:
Makes each row a group containing the rows of `table` whose `reference` field names it. A
group draws as a container around its members, with its label as a title in its header.
Diagrams only.

shadow.description:
Whether each block or group casts a shadow on the sheet, styled by the theme's
`diagram.shadow`. Default `false`. Diagrams only.

color.description:
Each row's color. Unset, rows take the theme's default for the mark; faces instead
blend their corners' colors.

visible.description: Whether each row is drawn and can be picked. Default `true`.

priority.description:
Each row's priority, from its data alone (no view state). Higher-priority rows draw
on top, are the last dropped when a table too large to draw whole is thinned to the
tiles in view, and are labeled first.

name.description: Distinguishes two marks of the same table across scenes, and names the mark in hits.

pick.description:
Whether rows respond to hover, clicks, and picks. Unset, vertices, edges, faces, and
plot traces do, and geometry (areas, and lines along paths such as coasts, borders,
and roads) does not.

select.description: Whether clicking a row selects it. Default `true`.

drag.description:
Whether pressing and moving a row drags it, reported as
[`Event::Drag`](crate::Event), instead of panning the camera. Default `false`.

label.description: Each row's label: a text field, or label options.

legend.description:
A legend of the mark's colors at the view's bottom right, under this title: a ticked
colormap across its domain, a cell for each category, or a swatch beside each name
of a map's `categories`. `color` must map through a colormap with a fixed domain or
named categories; in a conditional, `otherwise` is searched before the cases.

Vertices.description: Rows drawn as markers: points of a map, nodes of a graph, blocks of a diagram.

ExprNode.description: A value for each row: a number, a boolean, a field's name, or a node that computes one.

from.description: The dataset and table the field is read from, joined by row id.

step.description:
For a sampled field, reads the last frame at or before the shown coordinate instead of
interpolating. Default `false`.

FieldNode.description:
A field's value in each row: from the mark's own table, or with `from`, from another
dataset's table joined by row id.

color.description: A CSS color, such as `#ffb000` or `rebeccapurple`.

StateNode.description: View state of each row, such as whether it is selected.

State.description:
View state of each row: `selected`, `hovered`, `pointer` (CSS pixels from a vertex to the
pointer), `elapsed` (seconds since the view was created), or `zoom` (the camera's zoom).

MissingNode.description: A missing value. An option that evaluates to missing uses the theme's value.

Unary.description:
An operation on one value. `sin` and `cos` take radians; `not` treats values above 0.5 as
true.

Binary.description:
An operation on two values: arithmetic, `min` and `max`, comparisons (1 for true, 0 for
false), and logic. `rem` is a floored remainder, which takes the sign of the divisor. `and` and
`or` treat values above 0.5 as true.

when.description: The cases, as `[condition, value]` pairs tried in order.

otherwise.description: The value where no condition holds.

WhenNode.description: The value of the first case whose condition holds, else `otherwise`.

is.description: The text field, and the text it must equal.

IsNode.description: Whether a text field equals a text exactly.

contains.description: The text field, and the text it must contain.

ContainsNode.description:
Whether a text field contains a text, ignoring case. In a mark, the field must belong to the
mark's own table.

domain.description: The values mapped to the range's ends; the extent of the values shown when unset.

ScaleNode.description: A value mapped linearly onto a range, clamped to the range.

value.description: The value mapped. A categorical map takes each value's integer part as its category.

domain.description:
The values mapped to the colormap's ends; the extent of the values shown when unset. A
categorical map ignores it.

ColormapNode.description: A value mapped through a colormap.

Colormap.description: Colors for a range of values: a catalog name, or your own colors.

anyOf.description: A CSS color, such as `#ffb000` or `rebeccapurple`.

prefixItems.description: A CSS color, such as `#ffb000` or `rebeccapurple`.

colors.description:
The colors, blended in OKLab. Each is a color, spaced evenly between its neighbors as in a
CSS gradient, or a `[place, color]` pair with a place from 0 to 1, in ascending order. A
categorical map takes one color per category, without places, at most 256.

categories.description: The category names in category order, shown in legends. Categorical maps only.

CustomColormap.description: A custom colormap: its kind, its colors, and for a categorical map, its category names.

oneOf.description: Low to high.
Below and above a midpoint.
Around a circle: values wrap.
Distinct colors for distinct integers.

ColormapKind.description:
How a colormap maps values: `sequential` and `diverging` maps clamp, `cyclic` maps wrap, and
`categorical` maps give each integer its own color.

Size.description: A size: a value in the space's unit (units in a diagram, CSS pixels elsewhere), `{ px }` in CSS pixels, or `{ units }` in position units (degrees on the earth), which grow on screen as the view zooms in.

Px.description: A size in CSS pixels, regardless of the space's unit.

atLeast.description: The minimum on-screen size in CSS pixels, however far the view zooms out.

atMost.description: The maximum on-screen size in CSS pixels, however far the view zooms in.

Units.description:
A size in position units (degrees on the earth), regardless of the space's unit, so it scales
as the view zooms. `atLeast` and `atMost` bound it in CSS pixels.

oneOf.description: A filled shape.
A rectangle with rounded corners that holds its label inside, as a diagram's blocks do.

corner.description:
Corner radius in the space's unit (units in a diagram, CSS pixels elsewhere); the
theme's `diagram.corner` unless set.

oneOf.description: A shape's outline, filled to `fill` from 0 to 1: around a circle, or upward in other shapes.

fill.description: How full each row's gauge is, from 0 to 1.

shape.description: The outline's shape; an ellipse by default.

oneOf.description: A circle divided into slices sized in proportion to their values.

items.description: A CSS color, such as `#ffb000` or `rebeccapurple`.

hole.description: The hole in the middle, as a fraction of the radius; 0 by default.

oneOf.description: One of `images`, fitted to the marker's box; `index` picks the image for each row.

A custom marker in WGSL. `source` defines `fn marker(f: MarkerFragment) -> MarkerColor`,
which can read up to eight `inputs` as `f.input[i]`. It compiles once, when the view first
draws it.

source.description: The WGSL source of the `marker` function.

inputs.description: Each row's inputs, at most eight.

Marker.description:
How a vertex is drawn: a shape's name, `"block"`, or
`{ shape | block | gauge | pie | icon | wgsl: options }`. An ellipse by default.

oneOf.description: An ellipse: a circle when its width and height are equal.
A rectangle.
A rectangle with rounded corners.
A diamond.

Bitmap.description: An image of RGBA texels: straight alpha, sRGB, rows top to bottom.

PaintNode.description: A color for each row: a CSS color, a value through a colormap, or a conditional choosing between colors.

anyOf.description: A CSS color, such as `#ffb000` or `rebeccapurple`.

when.description: The cases, as `[condition, color]` pairs tried in order.

otherwise.description: The color where no condition holds.

WhenPaintNode.description: A conditional color: the color of the first case whose condition holds, else `otherwise`.

side.description: The side of the marker it sits on.

order.description:
Its position among the ports on its side, counted from the top or left. Ports without an
`order` follow those with one, in declaration order.

label.description: Its name, drawn beside it inside the marker.

shape.description: Its shape; an ellipse by default.

output.description: Whether it is an output, which drives its net. Default `false`, an input.

Port.description:
A port on one side of a vertex's marker, where a net connects: a side name, or options. The
vertex names the net in a reference field. An output drives its net: layouts rank a net from its
outputs, and the net's arrows point away from them.

```
# use latkit::{Port, Side, Vertices};
let pumps = Vertices::of("plant", "Pump").port("in", Side::Left).port("out", Port::output(Side::Right));
```

oneOf.description: The left side.
The right side.
The top.
The bottom.

size.description:
Font size in the space's unit (units in a diagram, CSS pixels elsewhere); the theme's
`text.size` unless set.

color.description: Each row's text color; the theme's text color unless set.

priority.description: Where labels would overlap, the higher priority shows; the mark's `priority` unless set.

maxWidth.description:
The width at which lines wrap, in the space's unit (units in a diagram, CSS pixels
elsewhere).

font.description: The CSS font family list for the text; the theme's `text.font` unless set.

max.description:
The most labels shown at once: those of highest priority among the rows in view, or fewer
where they would overlap. No limit unless set.

Label.description:
Text for each row, placed beside, inside, or along the row's shape and following it every frame:
a text field, or options. Where labels would overlap, the higher priority shows; among equals,
labels already shown stay. In a diagram a label is part of the drawing: it scales with the zoom,
fades out when too small to read, and shows wherever it fits its vertex.

```
# use latkit::{field, Label, Vertices};
let buses = Vertices::of("grid", "Bus").position("lon", "lat").label(Label::new("name").priority(field("kv")));
```

ends.description: The reference fields naming each row's two vertices.

bends.description: A path field whose points each row passes through between its ends.

route.description:
How each row runs between its ends: geodesic on the earth and straight elsewhere unless set.
`orthogonal` routes around blocks with rounded bends, in diagrams only.

arrows.description:
Whether each row has an arrowhead at its second end; a net has one at each input it reaches.
Default `false`.

poles.description:
Draws each row as a pole from its own vertex down to the ground, on a plane or the earth.
Poles take no `ends`, `bends`, or `joins`. Default `false`.

joins.description:
Draws each row as a net on a plane or the earth, joining the vertex rows of `table` whose
`reference` field names it: a star from their center to each member.

width.description:
Each row's width, in the space's unit (units in a diagram, CSS pixels elsewhere)
unless given with `px` or `units`. The theme's width unless set.

dash.description: Whether each row is dashed, with the theme's `dash` period. Default `false`.

flow.description:
The speed of comets flowing along each row, per second, in the unit of the theme's
`flow` lengths. Negative speeds flow backward; 0, the default, draws no comets. When
the speed changes, comets continue from where they are.

color.description:
Each row's color. Unset, rows take the theme's default for the mark; faces instead
blend their corners' colors.

visible.description: Whether each row is drawn and can be picked. Default `true`.

priority.description:
Each row's priority, from its data alone (no view state). Higher-priority rows draw
on top, are the last dropped when a table too large to draw whole is thinned to the
tiles in view, and are labeled first.

name.description: Distinguishes two marks of the same table across scenes, and names the mark in hits.

pick.description:
Whether rows respond to hover, clicks, and picks. Unset, vertices, edges, faces, and
plot traces do, and geometry (areas, and lines along paths such as coasts, borders,
and roads) does not.

select.description: Whether clicking a row selects it. Default `true`.

drag.description:
Whether pressing and moving a row drags it, reported as
[`Event::Drag`](crate::Event), instead of panning the camera. Default `false`.

label.description: Each row's label: a text field, or label options.

legend.description:
A legend of the mark's colors at the view's bottom right, under this title: a ticked
colormap across its domain, a cell for each category, or a swatch beside each name
of a map's `categories`. `color` must map through a colormap with a fixed domain or
named categories; in a conditional, `otherwise` is searched before the cases.

Edges.description: Rows drawn as strokes between the vertices named by two reference fields: branches, links, wires. In a diagram, a row without ends is a net, joining every vertex port whose reference field names it.

oneOf.description: A straight line on screen.
Along the great circle, on the earth.

Horizontal and vertical runs around vertices that leave and enter at their sides, with
rounded bends. Diagrams only.

Route.description: How an edge runs between its ends.

corners.description:
The reference fields naming each row's three vertices; required. Without a color, a face
blends the colors of its corners.

blend their corners' colors.

legend.description:
A legend of the mark's colors at the view's bottom right, under this title: a ticked
colormap across its domain, a cell for each category, or a swatch beside each name
of a map's `categories`. `color` must map through a colormap with a fixed domain or

Faces.description: Rows drawn as triangles between the vertices named by three reference fields: meshes, surfaces, and fields interpolated across a network. Faces are lit from the camera, so a flat mesh seen from above shows its exact colors.

geometry.description:
The path or polygon field each row runs along; the field named `geometry` by default. Not
allowed on a plot.

trace.description:
The sampled field each row traces across the data's axis; plots only, where it is required.
A field with no frames yet draws nothing until its first frame arrives.

interpolation.description: How each row runs between its samples on a plot; `linear` by default.

width.description:
Each row's width, in the space's unit (units in a diagram, CSS pixels elsewhere)
unless given with `px` or `units`. The theme's width unless set.

dash.description: Whether each row is dashed, with the theme's `dash` period. Default `false`.

`flow` lengths. Negative speeds flow backward; 0, the default, draws no comets. When
the speed changes, comets continue from where they are.

named categories; in a conditional, `otherwise` is searched before the cases.

Lines.description: Rows drawn as lines along a path field (roads, rivers, borders) or a polygon field's rings (area outlines). On a plot, each row instead traces a sampled field's history across the data's axis, as a monitor does. On the earth, paths follow the globe's curve and stay whole across the antimeridian.

oneOf.description: Straight from each sample to the next.

Each value holds from the previous sample up to its own, so the line steps at the previous
sample.
Each value holds until the next sample, where the line steps.

Interpolation.description: How a line runs between its samples.

geometry.description:
The polygon field each row fills, holding one polygon's rings or several polygons; the field
named `geometry` by default.

color.description:

blend their corners' colors.

Areas.description: Rows drawn as the areas of a polygon field: parcels, states, lakes, the land and water of a map. The view triangulates each row's polygons once, in the background when they are large. On the earth, areas follow the globe's curve and stay whole across the antimeridian. To outline areas, add a [`Lines`](crate::Lines) mark of the same table, which draws their rings.

oneOf.description: Drawn distances follow graph distances.
Ranks along a direction, for flows and hierarchies.

Layout.description:
How the view places vertex rows that have no position: a name, or
`{ stress | layered: options }`. In a diagram it places blocks; on a plane or the earth it
places points among the rows they link to. Gaps are in position units: diagram units, plane
units, or degrees on the earth.

A row keeps its place once placed: rows added later are placed around the others, and
[`View::arrange`](crate::View::arrange) lays out every row again.

gap.description: Distance between the centers of linked vertices, in position units. Default 40.

Stress.description:
Stress majorization: vertices move until drawn distances match graph distances, then overlapping
boxes separate, keeping a quarter of `gap` between them.

flow.description: The direction edges point; `right` by default.

gap.description: Distance between vertices within a rank, in position units. Default 30.

rankGap.description: Distance between ranks, in position units. Default 80.

Layered.description:
Layered drawing: vertices in ranks, edges pointing along `flow`, and nets ranked from their
outputs.

oneOf.description: Toward the right.
Toward the left.
Toward the bottom.
Toward the top.

grid.description: The color of a plane's or diagram's grid, a plot's grid lines, and the earth's graticule.

missing.description: The color a colormap gives a missing value, such as a row whose field has none.

dash.description: The dash period: one dash and one gap of equal length.

shading.description: How much faces darken as they turn away from the camera, from 0 to 1.

text.description: How labels, axis ticks, and titles look.

edge.description: Defaults for edges, and how parallel edges and arrowheads look.

focus.description: How hovered and selected rows glow, and how rows outside a selection dim.

flow.description: How comets flowing along edges and lines look.

diagram.description: How a diagram's blocks, groups, ports, and wires look.

base.description: The theme these options change; dark unless set.

Theme.description:
Default colors and sizes for marks whose options leave them unset or missing, and the look of
text, focus, comets, and each space, grouped by subject. Write a base theme's name (`"dark"` or
`"light"`), or options over a base (`base`, dark by default); a group's options override only
the base values they set.

Lengths are in the space's unit (units in a diagram, CSS pixels elsewhere), except the text halo
and the focus glow, which are always in CSS pixels.

size.description: The font size, in the space's unit.

halo.description: Width of the background-colored halo around label text, in CSS pixels.

TextTheme.description: How labels, axis ticks, and titles look.

radius.description: The vertex radius, in the space's unit.

color.description:
The edge color. `None` blends the colors of each edge's two vertices; a diagram's wires and
edges without `ends` (nets and poles) then take the text color.

width.description: The edge width, in the space's unit.

spacing.description:
In a diagram, the distance between edges joining the same two vertices and between parallel
orthogonal wires. Wires keep twice this distance from blocks where they can.

bow.description:
Outside a diagram, how far edges joining the same two vertices bow apart: each lane by this
fraction of the edge's length at its middle. A family spreads at most eight lanes wide, and
more lanes pack closer. A bow is part of the drawing, so it scales with the zoom.

arrow.description: How far an arrowhead extends beyond the edge's width: a head is this plus the width long.

EdgeTheme.description: Defaults for edges, and how parallel edges and arrowheads look.

width.description: The line width, in the space's unit.

hover.description: The glow color around hovered rows.

selected.description: The glow color around selected rows; `None` glows in each row's own color.

glow.description: How far the hover and selection glows reach, in CSS pixels.

dim.description: The opacity of rows outside the selection while any row is selected, from 0 to 1.

grow.description:
The scale factor for a hovered vertex sized in CSS pixels; vertices sized in units only
glow.

FocusTheme.description: How hovered and selected rows glow, and how rows outside a selection dim.

color.description:
The comet color. Its alpha sets how strongly a comet covers its stroke; a fully transparent
color turns comets off.

length.description: The length of a comet's tail behind its head.

width.description: The width of a comet's head, in the space's unit; never narrower than its stroke.

FlowTheme.description:
How comets flowing along edges and lines look: a round head, brightest at its middle, trailing a
tail that thins and fades.

`spacing` and `length` must be in the same unit, which also measures each row's `flow` speed. In
position units (degrees on the earth), comets are part of the drawing: they scale with the zoom
and stay in place along their lines. In CSS pixels, they keep their on-screen size and speed. A
plain number is in the space's unit.

Length.description: A length: a number in the space's unit (units in a diagram, CSS pixels elsewhere), `{ px }` in CSS pixels, or `{ units }` in position units (degrees on the earth), which grow on screen as the view zooms in.

units.description: Position units (degrees on the earth), which grow on screen as the view zooms in.

group.description: The fill color of group containers.

outline.description: The color of the one-unit border around blocks and groups; `None` draws no border.

corner.description: The corner radius of blocks and groups; a block marker can set its own.

bend.description: The bend radius of orthogonal wires.

groupPadding.description: The space between a group's members and its border.

shadow.description: How blocks and groups cast shadows on the sheet.

DiagramTheme.description: How a diagram's blocks, groups, ports, and wires look.

color.description: The color a shadow darkens toward; its alpha sets how dark the shadow is under the block.

lift.description: How far a shadow falls below its block or group; its edge softens over the same distance.

ShadowTheme.description: How a diagram's blocks and groups cast shadows on the sheet, for vertex marks with `shadow` on.

atmosphere.description: The color of the air glowing around the globe, when the earth's `atmosphere` is on.

night.description: The brightness of the night side when the earth has `daylight`, from 0 to 1.

playhead.description: The color of the line at the view's current axis coordinate.

pan.description: Whether dragging the background pans the camera. Default `true`.

zoom.description:
Which input zooms the view: the wheel and pinching (`wheel`, the default); pinching, and the
wheel only with Control or Meta held, as trackpad pinches send it, so the plain wheel
scrolls the page (`modifier`); or nothing (`off`).

turn.description:
Whether dragging with the secondary button, or with Shift, rotates and tilts a map or plane.
Default `true`.

keyboard.description:
Whether the keyboard controls the view. Default `true`. Tab and Shift+Tab step through the
rows nearest the view's center, and arrow keys step to the nearest row in their direction.
Enter opens the stepped-to row and Space selects it. With no row stepped to, arrow keys pan
(Shift+arrows turn), `+` and `-` zoom, Home fits everything, and Escape clears the
selection.

hover.description:
Whether the hovered row glows, and a hovered vertex sized in CSS pixels grows. Default
`true`. Rows are hovered either way: [`Event::Hovered`](crate::Event) still fires and
`hovered()` still reads them.

pickRadius.description:
How far from the pointer, in CSS pixels, a row can be and still be picked; touch adds 8.
Default 6.

selectBox.description:
Whether Shift+drag selects the rows inside a box instead of turning the camera. Shift+click
still toggles one row. Default `false`.

connect.description:
Whether the user can draw connections, reported as [`Event::Connect`](crate::Event): by
dragging from a port, from a vertex with Alt held, or an edge's end off its vertex. Default
`false`.

delete.description:
Whether Delete and Backspace report the selection as [`Event::Delete`](crate::Event).
Default `false`.

cycle.description:
Whether clicking again at the same point, with the camera unmoved, selects the next row
under it, nearest first, so overlapping rows can each be selected. Default `false`.

press.description:
Seconds a touch or pen must hold still to request a menu ([`Event::Menu`](crate::Event)),
as the secondary button does; 0 turns this off. Default 0.5.

motion.description:
How much the view animates on its own: eases, camera flights, coasting, orbits, label fades,
comets, and options that read `elapsed()`. `system` (the default) follows the user's
reduced-motion setting, `full` animates everything, and `reduced` animates only motion the
user drives.

Controls.description:
How a view responds to the pointer and keyboard, and how much it animates on its own: a preset
(`"none"` or `"inspect"`), or options over the defaults. Each mark controls whether its own rows
pick, select, and drag; these options control the view itself.

oneOf.description: The wheel, pinching, and the keys.

Pinching and the keys, and the wheel only with Control or Meta held (as trackpad pinches
send it), so the plain wheel scrolls the page.
No input zooms.
Follows the system: reduced when the user asked their system for less motion.
All motion.

Only motion the user drives: changes apply at once, flights jump, nothing coasts or orbits,
labels appear without fading, and comets and options that read `elapsed()` stay still.

Motion.description: How much a view animates on its own.

Data.description: A dataset's JSON document: its name and the patch that builds it.

oneOf.description: Sets the axis that sampled fields are recorded over, such as `time` in `s`.

fields.description: Fields by name, in the order written.

additionalProperties.description: A field's values: an array of one kind of value; a reference naming another table's rows by id; or a slice of a binary file beside the document.

oneOf.description: Replaces a table with these rows and fields, or adds it.

fields.description: Fields by name, in the order written.

additionalProperties.description: A field's values: an array of one kind of value; a reference naming another table's rows by id; or a slice of a binary file beside the document.

oneOf.description:
Writes fields for these rows. Rows with existing ids are updated, new ids add rows, and
fields left out keep their values. A missing table is added.
Removes the rows with these ids; ids that match no row are ignored.

fields.description: Fields by name, in the order written.

additionalProperties.description: A field's values: an array of one kind of value; a reference naming another table's rows by id; or a slice of a binary file beside the document.

oneOf.description:
Records a frame at each axis coordinate in `at`. Each field gives one value per row per
coordinate, frame-major. Covers every row, or only the rows `ids` names; other rows keep
their last values.
Forgets every sampled field's frames before axis coordinate `before`.

Inserts a run of entries of sampled field `field` at level `level`, numbered from `first`,
as time tiles store them. At level 0 each entry is a frame: one coordinate in `at` and one
value per row in `values`. At level `k` each entry is a bucket of `8^k` frames: its first
and last frame's coordinates in `at`, and in `values` every bucket's least value per row,
followed by every bucket's greatest. Null is missing.

Change.description: One change in a patch, keyed by the name of the `Patch` method that makes it.

Ids.description: Row ids: a list of numbers or texts, or `{count}` for rows 0 to count - 1. In a reference, null names no row.

count.description: The number of rows, whose ids are 0 to count - 1.

Id.description: A row's id: a whole number from 0, or a text. A number above 2^53 - 1 is written as its decimal text, which names the same row.

Value.description: One value: a number, boolean, text, or geometry; null, or an empty geometry, is missing.

Geometry.description: A point `[x, y]` (a third coordinate is ignored), or a list of geometries one level down: a path is a list of points, parts a list of paths, and polygons a list of parts.

Dtype.description:
The value type of a slice's bytes. Numbers are little endian; `bool` is one byte each, nonzero
meaning true.

ids.description:
The rows to read, in this order unless sorted; every row when unset. Ids that name no row
are skipped.

filter.description: Keeps only the rows for which this is true.

sort.description:
Keys to sort by, each breaking ties left by the keys before it. Rows where a key has no
value sort last; rows equal on every key keep their order.

offset.description: How many of the kept rows to skip.

limit.description:
The most rows to return. When sorting with a limit, the first `offset + limit` rows are
selected in linear time and only those are sorted.

select.description:
Fields to return, by output name. A plain field returns that field as stored; any other
expression returns numbers. Every field when unset; an empty object returns the ids alone.

at.description: The axis coordinate at which sampled fields are read; their last frame when unset.

Query.description: The rows of a table to read back, run through the expressions marks draw with.

oneOf.description: Smallest first.
Largest first.

Order.description: Sort direction. Rows where the key has no value sort last in either direction.

range.description: The axis range the spans cover, `[first, last]`: finite, with `first <= last`.

spans.description: The number of equal spans to divide the range into; at least 1.

ids.description: The rows to read, in this order; every row when unset.

EnvelopeRequest.description:
A request for each row's least and greatest value of a sampled field over equal spans of the
axis: field `field` of table `table`, over `spans` equal spans from `range[0]` to `range[1]`,
for every row or for the rows `ids` names, in that order. Plain data that deserializes from
JSON, like a query.

center.description:
Longitude, latitude, and elevation on the earth; x, y, and elevation on a plane or a
diagram. In JSON, `[x, y]` is shorthand for elevation 0.

zoom.description: The web mercator zoom level on the earth; elsewhere, log₂ of CSS pixels per unit.

pitch.description: Tilt in degrees from looking straight down, up to 75. Ignored in a diagram.

bearing.description: Degrees clockwise from north, or from up on a plane. Ignored in a diagram.

anyOf.description:
A camera over the earth, a plane, or a diagram: the point it looks at and turns about, its
zoom, its tilt, and its rotation. A diagram is always seen from straight above, upright.

y.description: The value range shown, or `None` to fit the values in view.

anyOf.description: A plot camera: the x range shown, and the value range, or `None` to fit the values in view.

oneOf.description: Everything drawn.
These rows.
Brings this row into view, keeping the zoom.
The box from `min` to `max`: x, y, and elevation.

Fit.description: The target of a view's fit.

ids.description: The rows' ids in the table.

Rows.description:
Rows of one table in a dataset, by id. Views use it for selections, fits, and the rows events
report.

id.description: The row's id in the table.

Row.description:
One row, identified by dataset name, table name, and id. It stays valid across any change that
keeps those names and the id.

bytes.description:
GPU memory in bytes for the data all views of the `Gpu` draw: its pages and each view's
per-row state. A view draws a table too large for its share as a paged table, drawing only
the pages the camera needs, so it always fits. Pages no view draws stay cached in the
remaining room, least recently drawn evicted first. Defaults to half the device's largest
storage buffer. The page pool grows as data needs it and never shrinks, so set the budget
before drawing data.

uploadPerFrame.description:
Most bytes uploaded per frame; larger data streams in over several frames. Defaults to
32 MiB.

Budget.description: How much GPU memory latkit uses.

scale.description: Pixels per CSS pixel. Views lay out `size / scale` CSS pixels. Defaults to 1.

panels.description:
Each view's panel, `[x, y, width, height]` as fractions of the picture. Defaults to one view
filling it.

transparent.description: Whether the picture keeps alpha where the themes' backgrounds would be.

capture.description: When the picture is taken: once its views are complete and still, or as they are now.

elapsed.description:
Fixed effect time in seconds for elapsed-time expressions and flowing comets. `None` follows
the view's clock.

oneOf.description:
Once every view is complete and still. Transitions, camera flights, and label fades advance
1/60 s per step until they finish.
Once every view is complete, as it is now. Anything in motion is captured where it is.
A row was clicked.
A row was double-clicked, or Enter was pressed on the row the keyboard points at.

hits.description: The rows under the point, nearest first.

oneOf.description:
A context menu was requested: by a secondary click, the menu key, or a touch or pen held
still. Lists the rows under the trigger's point, for a menu of actions on them.

phase.description: Whether the drag starts, moves, or ends.

hit.description: The row dragged, as it was hit.

position.description:
The row's new position in the space's coordinates: the hit point moved with the pointer
since the press, at the depth where the drag started, so a vertex keeps its grab offset.
Snapped to a diagram's dots when its grid snaps.

oneOf.description:
A row of a draggable mark is dragged. The drag starts once the pointer moves more than 4 CSS
pixels from where it pressed the row.

from.description: The end it was drawn from: for an edge, the end that stayed.

to.description: The vertex it was released over, if any.

edge.description: The edge whose end was dragged off; `to` replaces that end.

oneOf.description:
A connection was drawn with [`Controls::connect`](crate::Controls) on: from a port, from a
vertex with Alt held, or by dragging an edge's end off it.

Delete or Backspace was pressed with rows selected and [`Controls::delete`](crate::Controls)
on.

hit.description: The row now hovered; `None` once no row is.

oneOf.description: The hovered row changed: [`View::hovered`](crate::View::hovered).

trigger.description: How the user changed it; `None` when the data dropped rows from it.

oneOf.description: The selection changed: [`View::selection`](crate::View::selection).

The camera moved by a gesture, fit, flight, coast, or orbit:
[`View::camera`](crate::View::camera).

The work the last frame waited on changed; empty once frames are complete:
[`View::waiting`](crate::View::waiting).

Something failed; reported once. A mark that no longer fits its data is also listed in
[`View::failures`](crate::View::failures).

ViewEvent.description: Something that happened in a view, as [`View::events`](crate::View::events) reports it.

mark.description: The name of the mark that drew it, if named. It tells two marks of one table apart.

point.description:
The row's point nearest the probe, in CSS pixels from the top left: a vertex's or port's
middle, or the nearest point of a stroke or triangle.

position.description: That point in the space's coordinates: x, y, and elevation.

distance.description: CSS pixels from the probe to the row.

port.description: The port hit, when a vertex's port was.

sample.description: The sample hit, when a line tracing a sampled field was.

Hit.description: A row under a point, as the frame drew it.

id.description: The row's id in the table.

Row.description:
One row, identified by dataset name, table name, and id. It stays valid across any change that
keeps those names and the id.

Id.description: A row's id: a whole number from 0, or a text. A number above 2^53 - 1 is written as its decimal text, which names the same row.

frame.description: The frame, numbered from the first ever recorded. JSON uses a decimal string above 2^53 - 1.

Sample.description: A sample of a traced field: its frame, the axis coordinate it was recorded at, and its value.

point.description: CSS pixels from the top left.

Trigger.description:
Where the user acted, with which modifier keys, and with which device. For keyboard input, the
point is the row the keys point at, else the pointer, else the view's middle.

Modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during an input.

oneOf.description: A mouse or a trackpad.
A pen.
A finger: picks reach 8 CSS pixels farther.
The keyboard.
The pointer moved far enough to drag.
The pointer moved.
The pointer was released, or the drag was cancelled.

port.description: The port, by the reference field naming its net.

End.description: A vertex a connection ends at, and the port the connection meets, if any.

ids.description: The rows' ids in the table.

Rows.description:
Rows of one table in a dataset, by id. Views use it for selections, fits, and the rows events
report.

center.description:
Longitude, latitude, and elevation on the earth; x, y, and elevation on a plane or a
diagram. In JSON, `[x, y]` is shorthand for elevation 0.

zoom.description: The web mercator zoom level on the earth; elsewhere, log₂ of CSS pixels per unit.

pitch.description: Tilt in degrees from looking straight down, up to 75. Ignored in a diagram.

bearing.description: Degrees clockwise from north, or from up on a plane. Ignored in a diagram.

anyOf.description:
A camera over the earth, a plane, or a diagram: the point it looks at and turns about, its
zoom, its tilt, and its rotation. A diagram is always seen from straight above, upright.

y.description: The value range shown, or `None` to fit the values in view.

anyOf.description: A plot camera: the x range shown, and the value range, or `None` to fit the values in view.

Waiting.description: What a frame still waits on: pipelines the scene draws with, which compile before the view draws anything new (`compiling`); pages uploading, or tables not yet built from them (`data`); layouts, routes, lanes, shapes, tiles, or pyramids (`derived`); label placement, or text not yet set (`labels`); a fit due or being measured (`fit`); segment counts, or a transition starting (`marks`). Empty once the frame is complete.

Failure.description: What failed, as JSON: the form of the npm package's `LatkitError`.

code.description: The kind of failure, as `LatkitError.code` describes it.

path.description: The invalid part of the input, such as `marks[2].vertices.color`, on `invalid` failures.

drawn.description:
Rows every mark draws: every row of a table drawn whole, and the rows of the tiles in view
of a paged table.

draws.description: Draw calls the last frame recorded, label draws included.

instances.description:
Instances the last frame's draws drew: points, segments, triangles, and glyphs. An upper
bound for segments, which the GPU may cull.

tiles.description: Fetched tiles the view draws, of every tile source.

tilesLoading.description: Tiles being fetched or decoded, of every tile source.

cpuMs.description: Milliseconds the last frame took to record on the CPU.

gpuMs.description:
Milliseconds the GPU takes per frame: the median of recently measured frames; 0 if the
device cannot measure.

uploads.description:
Data pages, or pieces of pages, uploaded. A change's uploads count pages here and bytes in
`uploaded`.

written.description: Bytes written other than pages: uniforms, programs, label runs, the selection, and textures.

evaluated.description: Rows whose channels the GPU evaluated.

resolved.description:
Edge and face rows whose endpoints the GPU resolved to their vertices' resident rows: rows
that changed, plus every row of a page that references a vertex now resident elsewhere.

cleared.description:
Bytes of per-row word pages the GPU cleared: pages read before anything writes them, and the
normals that faces sum from scratch.

packed.description:
Rows packed into pages of a paged table's draw order. Each page is packed once, the first
time a view draws it, and again only when a write changes its rows.

readbacks.description:
Readbacks from the GPU: probes, queries, fits, label placements, segment counts, and
pictures. Frame timer readbacks, which only some devices support, are not counted.

jobs.description:
Jobs started: layouts, routes, lanes, triangulations, pyramids, and tiles. They run on the
host's workers, or immediately without a host.

texts.description: Label texts the host was asked to rasterize.

pipelines.description:
Pipelines compiled. In a browser, each compiles in the background when a view or shot
requests it ahead of use. Natively, each compiles when first created.

late.description:
Pipelines not requested ahead of use, compiled when first used. In a browser they compile
on the GPU's thread and delay frames. Zero unless a scene uses a pipeline it did not
request.

Work.description:
Counts of the work a [`Gpu`](crate::Gpu) has done since it was created. Subtract two
snapshots to get the work between them.

axis.description: The axis name and unit, if set.

span.description: The first and last axis coordinates held by any sampled field; `None` when none holds any.

recorded over, and the part of the axis they cover.

TableDescription.description: A summary of one table: its row count and its fields, sorted by name.

kind.description: The kind of values it holds.

to.description: For a reference, the target table.

span.description: For a sampled field, the first and last axis coordinates it holds.

FieldDescription.description: A summary of one field: its kind, plus its target table or axis span where those apply.
